question: A 67-year-old woman presents to the infectious disease clinic after her PPD was found to be positive. A subsequent chest radiography shows a cavity in the apex of the right upper lobe, along with significant hilar adenopathy. The patient is diagnosed with tuberculosis and is started on the standard four-drug treatment regimen. Four weeks later, she returns for her first follow-up appointment in panic because her eyes have taken on an orange/red hue. Which of the following describes the mechanism of action of the drug most likely responsible for this side effect?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Tuberculosis treatment" -> "Standard four-drug regimen" -> "Likely includes isoniazid" -> "Isoniazid can cause orange/red discoloration of eyes (ocular toxicity)" -> "Inhibition of mycolic acid synthesis" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Tuberculosis treatment" -> "Standard four-drug regimen" -> "Likely includes rifampin" -> "Rifampin can cause orange/red discoloration of body fluids, including tears" -> "Inhibition of RNA polymerase" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The drug most likely responsible for the orange/red hue in the patient's eyes is rifampin, which inhibits RNA polymerase. This is supported by the fact that rifampin can cause orange/red discoloration of body fluids, including tears, as a known side effect.
analysis: The patient is experiencing a common side effect of rifampin, one of the standard drugs used in the treatment of tuberculosis. Rifampin is known to cause bodily fluids, including tears and urine, to turn an orange/red color. The mechanism of action of rifampin is the inhibition of bacterial RNA polymerase, which prevents RNA synthesis and thus bacterial replication.
